mainTopic: Court sales of orphans' property (pricing errors, the announcement rule, and selling movables), then a new משנה on which women lose their כתובה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב יוסף's point: a buyer at a court sale keeps his guarantee, and it rests on the orphans. Next, רב ששת says that according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a court's sale stands even if the price was off by up to half, and a ברייתא supports this. אמימר quotes רב יוסף: a court that sold without a public announcement (הכרזה) has made a mistake in a clear rule, so the sale is reversed. רב אשי challenges this from a משנה, and the גמרא gives three answers. Some items (slaves, movables, documents) are never announced. Urgent needs (head tax, food, burial) allow selling without an announcement. And some places, like נהרדעא, never announced at all. The גמרא then teaches how orphans' movable property is sold: at the market if market day is near, right away if it is far. Two stories with רב כהנא and רבינא show this. Finally, a new משנה lists women who get no כתובה (ממאנת, שניה, איילונית) and women in forbidden marriages who still do. The גמרא begins with רב and שמואל arguing about a minor divorced with a גט, and שמואל's list of differences between a ממאנת and a divorcée continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why רב יוסף needed to say the buyer still gets a guarantee
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why רב יוסף's ruling is not obvious. One might think a buyer from a court gives up his guarantee because court sales are public. רב יוסף teaches that he does not give it up.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that anyone who buys from the court buys knowing the sale is made public, so he gives up his guarantee. That is why רב יוסף had to teach us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: Just before this line, the גמרא asked why רב יוסף's ruling (that the guarantee on a court sale rests on the orphans) needed to be said at all. Here it gives the answer: without his ruling we might have thought the buyer gives up his guarantee.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court sale is announced publicly, so a buyer might reason: 'If nobody came forward with a claim by now, the land is safe, and I don't need a guarantee.' The גמרא says this line of thinking is a real possibility, which is why רב יוסף had to say it. His teaching tells us the buyer keeps his guarantee, and it rests on the orphans, not on the court.

keyTerms.meaning: From the court
A 'voice,' meaning publicity or public knowledge
'He teaches us', meaning this is the new point being taught
A property guarantee: the seller's responsibility to pay back the buyer if the land is taken away

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ruling. It is the second half of a 'you might have thought' (מהו דתימא) answer that started just before. Read it as: 'You might have thought X, so רב יוסף teaches us that X is wrong.'

phrases.english: Anyone who buys from the court

phrases.aramaic: אַדַּעְתָּא לְמִיפַּק לֵיהּ קָלָא הוּא דְּזָבֵין,
phrases.english: buys with the understanding that the sale gets publicized,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to a 'פשיטא' challenge on רב יוסף's ruling from the previous section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows there was a reasonable mistaken assumption that the ruling comes to correct.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a court sale is public, the buyer gives up his guarantee.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer keeps his guarantee, and it rests on the orphans.
steps.whyThisMatters: It establishes that a buyer from a court sale keeps his guarantee even though the sale was public.

steps.title: How far can a court's price be off according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view in the משנה, that a court's sale stands even if they made a pricing mistake, and asks how big that mistake can be.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says (as in the משנה). And up to how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes the opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the משנה and asks a clarifying question about it, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the תנא קמא said that if the judges sold for a sixth too little or a sixth too much, the sale is cancelled. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagreed and said the sale stands, because of the authority of the court. But surely there is some limit, so the גמרא asks how large a mistake the court's authority can still cover.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.', meaning the rest of the quote from the משנה
'And up to how much?', asking for the limit

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says, etc.
phrases.notes: He says the court's sale stands even if they erred in the price, because otherwise what power would a court have?

phrases.english: And up to how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by returning to the next part of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum pricing error under which, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a court sale still stands.

steps.title: רב ששת: up to half
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the court's sale stands as long as the pricing mistake is up to half.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רב ששת: up to half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the previous step. The court's authority covers a mistake of up to half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a big mistake, up to half, does not cancel a court's sale according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. This is much more lenient than the sixth that the תנא קמא allows. Beyond that limit, the sale would not stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to half

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said
that Rav Sheshet said:
Up to half.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A court sale stands under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as long as the pricing error is up to half.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the 'up to half' limit
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: if a court sold something worth 200 for 100, or worth 100 for 200, the sale stands. This matches רב ששת's 'up to half.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said, a court that sold something worth two hundred for one hundred, or worth one hundred for two hundred, their sale stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling something worth 200 for only 100 means the price was off by half. Since the ברייתא picks this as its example and gives nothing bigger, it shows that half is the outer limit. This fits exactly with רב ששת's 'up to half.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught this way', introducing a ברייתא that supports what was just said
A coin unit equal to one hundred זוז
Their sale stands (is valid)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a court's sale stands even if the price was off by as much as half (for example, 200 sold for 100). This is רב ששת's view, and a ברייתא supports it.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
A court that sold
something worth two hundred for one hundred,
or something worth one hundred for two hundred,
their sale stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב ששת's answer in step 3 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's limit of 'up to half.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives the example of 200 sold for 100, a mistake of half, and says the sale stands.

steps.title: A court sale without a public announcement is reversed
steps.stepSummary: אמימר quotes רב יוסף: if a court sold without a public announcement, it is treated as a mistake about a clear rule, and the sale is undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said in the name of רב יוסף: a court that sold without an announcement is treated like judges who made a mistake in a clear rule of the משנה, and the sale is reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule about court sales. Skipping the public announcement cancels the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pricing mistake can be forgiven, as we just saw, but leaving out the announcement is a different kind of error. Judges who rule against a clear, known rule (טעה בדבר משנה) have their ruling undone. רב יוסף puts a sale without הכרזה into that category, so the sale is reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: A public announcement that the property is for sale
Made a mistake in a clear, known rule (as opposed to a judgment call)
'And they go back', meaning the decision is reversed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the pricing mistake of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A wrong price (up to half) can stand, but skipping the announcement is a mistake in a clear rule, so the sale is undone.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the public announcement is an essential part of a court sale, not just a good practice.

phrases.english: Ameimar said in the name of Rav Yosef:
A court that sold without an announcement
is treated like judges who erred in a matter of the Mishnah,
phrases.notes: He means a clear, known rule, not a matter of opinion. A mistake like that gets undone.

phrases.english: and the sale is reversed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from pricing mistakes to a new rule about the announcement requirement in court sales.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A court sale made without הכרזה counts as an error in a clear rule (טעה בדבר משנה), and the sale is reversed.

steps.title: Why 'treated as' a mistake? It is a real mistake!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב יוסף said the court is only 'treated as' making a mistake about a clear rule. A משנה openly requires announcements, so the court plainly made that kind of mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why say 'they are treated as if' they erred? They certainly erred! As we learned in a משנה: the appraisal for orphans' property is announced for thirty days, the appraisal for הקדש property is announced for sixty days, and they announce in the morning and in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of רב יוסף's ruling from the last step. It brings a משנה that clearly requires announcements, so a court that skipped them simply made a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the court is 'treated as' (נעשו) erring in a clear rule (טועה בדבר משנה). The גמרא says this is no mere 'as if': the משנה in ערכין openly requires announcing morning and evening. If that משנה already says this, what did רב יוסף add?

keyTerms.meaning: They are treated as / considered as
They certainly made a mistake
An appraisal of property before it is sold
Property dedicated to the בית המקדש
They publicly announce the sale

phrases.english: They are 'treated as if'? They certainly erred!
phrases.notes: This goes back to רב יוסף's words in the last step: 'it is treated as a mistake about a clear rule.'

phrases.english: As we learned: the appraisal of orphans' property is for thirty days,
and the appraisal of consecrated property is for sixty days,
and they announce in the morning and in the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רב יוסף's ruling quoted by אמימר in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's phrase 'נעשו כטועין' (treated as if they erred).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה openly requires announcements, so skipping them is plainly a mistake about a clear rule. The 'as if' wording is too weak, and the ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: That משנה could have been only about an agent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that from the ערכין משנה alone, one might think announcements are needed only when an agent sells, not when a court sells. רב יוסף teaches that a court needs them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If I had only that משנה, I would have said this applies only to an agent, but not to a court. So רב יוסף teaches us that it applies to a court too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב יוסף added. The ערכין משנה alone might be read as applying only to an agent, so רב יוסף teaches that a court must announce too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without רב יוסף, one could think a court is trusted enough that it does not need announcements, unlike an agent. רב יוסף teaches that even a court that skips the announcement has erred, and its sale is undone. So his ruling adds something new.

keyTerms.meaning: An agent who sells on someone else's behalf
A court
I would have thought

phrases.english: If from that one alone, I would have said
this applies to an agent,
but a court — no,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by showing what רב יוסף's ruling adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the earlier source is limited (agent only), so the new ruling adds something.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ערכין משנה requires announcements only from an agent, not from a court.
steps.terutzMaskana: A court must also announce. If it does not, its sale is undone, as רב יוסף taught.

steps.title: רב אשי: a fair-priced court sale stands, even without an announcement?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר from a teaching that a court sale is void only if the price is off by a sixth. This implies a sale at the right price stands, apparently even without an announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenged אמימר: when judges appraise and sell, if they went a sixth below the value or a sixth above it, the sale is void. That means if they sold at the true value, the sale stands. Isn't that talking about a case where they did not announce?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a source that seems to contradict רב יוסף's ruling as quoted by אמימר. It suggests a court sale at the right price stands, even with no announcement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching makes the court's sale depend only on the price. If they sold at the true value, it stands. רב אשי reads this as covering a sale with no announcement, which goes against the rule that such a sale is undone.

keyTerms.meaning: Judges
One-sixth
Their sale is void
At its exact value

phrases.english: Rav Ashi raised an objection to Ameimar:
The appraisal of the judges, where they went down by a sixth
or went up by a sixth — their sale is void.
So if at its exact value — their sale stands.
Is it not talking about where they did not announce?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against the ruling quoted by אמימר in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a court sale without an announcement is undone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The teaching implies a fair-priced court sale stands. If that covers a sale with no announcement, a missing announcement does not undo the sale.

steps.title: אמימר: that case had an announcement
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that the teaching is talking about a sale where the court did announce.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about where they announced.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר defends his ruling. He says the teaching is about a sale that was announced, so it says nothing about a sale with no announcement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case had an announcement, the only remaining question is the price. Then a sale at the true value standing does not contradict the rule that a sale without an announcement is undone.

keyTerms.meaning: Where they did announce

phrases.english: No, where they announced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the teaching is about an announced sale.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching is about a sale with no announcement.
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching is about a sale with an announcement, so it does not contradict רב יוסף.

steps.title: The last clause is the announced case, so the first clause is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on אמימר's answer. The last clause of the same teaching is clearly about an announced sale, so the first clause must be about a sale with no announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last clause is about where they announced, the first clause must be about where they did not announce. As the last clause teaches: if they made a public inspection notice, even if they sold something worth 100 for 200, or worth 200 for 100, their sale stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אמימר's answer from the structure of the teaching. The last clause openly deals with an announced sale, which leaves the first clause for a sale with no announcement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last clause says that with a public notice (אגרת בקורת), even a mistake of up to half still stands. So the first clause, where only a sixth undoes the sale, must be the case with no announcement. Yet it still says a sale at the true value stands, which goes against רב יוסף's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a teaching
The first clause of a teaching
A public inspection notice announcing the sale
A sum of one hundred (דינרים)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two clauses. The first clause (a sixth undoes the sale) is now the case with no announcement. The last clause (even half still stands) is the case with an announcement.

phrases.english: But since the last clause is where they announced,
the first clause is where they did not announce,
as the last clause teaches:
If they made an inspection notice,
phrases.notes: This is a public notice that lets buyers come and look the property over, so it counts as announcing.

phrases.english: even if they sold something worth one hundred for two hundred

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שָׁוֶה מָאתַיִם בְּמָנֶה — מִכְרָן קַיָּים.
phrases.english: or something worth two hundred for one hundred — their sale stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִדְּסֵיפָא בִּדְאַכְרוּז הָוֵי, רֵישָׁא בִּדְלָא אַכְרוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אמימר's answer in step 9 and brings back רב אשי's challenge from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's answer that the first clause is about an announced sale.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last clause openly covers the announced case with a wider allowance (up to half). So the first clause must be the unannounced case, and it still allows a fair-priced sale to stand.

steps.title: A new answer: some items are never announced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier answer. It agrees the teaching is about an unannounced sale, and explains that it deals with items that are normally sold without any announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the first clause really is about a sale with no announcement, and there is still no contradiction. אמימר is talking about items that are normally announced. The teaching is talking about items that are never announced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on saying the teaching is about an announced sale. It gives a new answer that splits the cases by the type of item being sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the גמרא showed that the first clause must be about a sale with no announcement. Now it accepts that point. The fix is that the teaching only covers items that are never announced, so a fair price is enough for them. אמימר's rule, that a sale without an announcement is void, covers items that do need an announcement.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and offers a new one)
Actually, really
They announced (here: did not announce)
Here... there (splits two sources into two different cases)
One announces (publicly declares a sale)

phrases.english: Rather, actually it is where they did not announce,
phrases.notes: This means the first clause of the teaching about the one-sixth price error, which step 10 showed is about an unannounced sale.

phrases.english: and it is not difficult:
here, with items that one announces,
phrases.notes: "Here" is אמימר's rule that a sale without an announcement is void.

phrases.english: there, with items that one does not announce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם בִּדְלָא אַכְרוּז, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the push-back of step 10 and replaces the answer of step 9 with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources by the type of item being sold
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching seemed to let any unannounced sale stand at a fair price, which would go against אמימר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only items that are never announced may be sold without an announcement. For items that are normally announced, אמימר's rule holds and the sale is void.

steps.title: The list of items that are not announced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the items that are sold without an announcement: slaves, movable property, and documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the items that are not announced: slaves, movable property, and documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out which items belong to the group 'items that are not announced' from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 depended on a category of items that are never announced. Here the גמרא fills in that category so we know exactly which sales it covers.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaves
Movable property
Documents (for example, loan documents)

phrases.english: And these are the items
that one does not announce:
slaves, movable property, and documents.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין מַכְרִיזִין עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the category that step 11's answer relies on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaves, movable property, and documents are sold without an announcement.

steps.title: Why are slaves not announced?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that slaves are sold without an announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that slaves are not announced?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to explain the list. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Announcing a sale protects the orphans by bringing in more buyers. So we need a reason to skip it for these items.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: Slaves, what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the list in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why slaves, and the other items on the list, are sold without an announcement.

steps.title: Announcing would put these items at risk
steps.stepSummary: Slaves might hear about the sale and run away. Movable property and documents might be stolen once people know about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Slaves might hear that they are being sold and run away. Movable property and documents might be stolen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: announcing these sales would put the property itself at risk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An announcement is meant to help the orphans get a better price. For these items, a public announcement would likely cause a loss, through escape or theft. So the court skips it and only makes sure the price is fair.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest, perhaps
They will run away
They will be stolen

phrases.english: Lest they hear and run away.
Movable property and documents —
lest they be stolen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An announcement would risk losing the property, through escape (slaves) or theft (movables and documents).
steps.whatToRemember: First answer: the teaching that lets a fair-priced sale stand without an announcement is about slaves, movable property, and documents. Those are never announced because of the risk of escape or theft.

steps.title: A second answer: times when there is no announcement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another answer. The difference is not the type of item but the situation: sometimes the court does not announce at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: אמימר is talking about a time when one announces. The teaching is talking about a time when one does not announce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to settle the contradiction between אמימר and the teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the split is by circumstance rather than by item. Even land, which is normally announced, may sometimes be sold without an announcement. In those times a fair-priced sale stands. The next step explains which times these are.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another answer)
At a time, in a situation

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
here, at a time when one announces,
there, at a time when one does not announce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, alongside the answer of step 11, to the problem raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources by situation (time of urgent need)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching seemed to let any unannounced sale stand, which would go against אמימר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching is about situations where announcing is not done. Normally, אמימר's rule applies.

steps.title: The Sages of נהרדעא: urgent needs allow selling without an announcement
steps.stepSummary: The Sages of נהרדעא rule that for head tax, food, and burial, the court sells without an announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Sages of נהרדעא say: to pay the head tax, to pay for food, and for burial, we sell without an announcement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the second answer by quoting the Sages of נהרדעא, who name the times when there is no announcement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An announcement takes time, and some needs cannot wait. Taxes must be paid, orphans must eat, and the dead must be buried. In these cases the court sells right away, and a fair price is enough for the sale to stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages of the city נהרדעא
Head tax (a tax on each person)
Food, sustenance
Burial
An announcement

phrases.english: As the Sages of Neharde'a say:
For head tax, for food, and for burial —
we sell without an announcement.
phrases.notes: "We" means the court, selling property the orphans inherited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 15 by defining 'a time when one does not announce.'
steps.raayaObject: The second answer: there are times when a court sells without an announcement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of the Sages of נהרדעא about head tax, food, and burial.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers for אמימר: (1) some items (slaves, movables, documents) are never announced; (2) in urgent times (head tax, food, burial) the court sells without an announcement. Otherwise, a court sale without an announcement is void.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical limits of the announcement rule. The rule protects orphans, but it gives way when announcing would cause a loss or when the need is urgent.

steps.title: It depends on the place: some places announce and some do not
steps.stepSummary: One source speaks about a place where the court announces sales. The other speaks about a place where the court does not announce at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: here it is a place where they announce, and there it is a place where they do not announce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to settle the conflict between the sources about announcing. The difference is the local custom, not the kind of item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer split the cases by the kind of item (step 11), and the second by the situation of urgent need (step 15). This third answer splits them by place: אמימר's rule is for a town where court sales are announced, and the משנה's first clause is for a town where they never announce. There, a fair-priced sale without an announcement stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
Here... there (each source is about a different case)
They announce (publicly declare the sale)

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
here, it is a place where they announce,
there, it is a place where they do not announce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer that settles the sources by local custom
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by place (local custom)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's first clause seemed to let an unannounced court sale at a fair price stand, which would go against אמימר's rule that such a sale is reversed.
steps.terutzMaskana: אמימר's rule applies in a place where court sales are announced. The משנה's first clause applies in a place where they are never announced, so there a fair-priced sale stands.

steps.title: רב נחמן: נהרדעא never made an announcement document
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן confirms that there really were places with no announcements. נהרדעא never made an אגרת בקורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן said: They never made a document of inspection in נהרדעא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the last answer by showing that a real place, נהרדעא, never announced court sales.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 17 depends on there being places with no announcements at all. רב נחמן's report proves such places existed. This makes the answer more than a guess.

keyTerms.meaning: Document of inspection (the court's public notice about property being sold)
Never, not even once
נהרדעא, a major Jewish city in Babylonia

phrases.english: As Rav Naḥman said:
They never made a document of inspection
in Neharde'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן מֵעוֹלָם לֹא עָשׂוּ אִגֶּרֶת בִּקּוֹרֶת בִּנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 17 with a real example
steps.raayaObject: That some places do not announce court sales at all

steps.title: The students guess the reason: the judges were expert appraisers
steps.stepSummary: Students understood that נהרדעא skipped announcements because its judges were experts at valuing property.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from it that this was because they were experts in appraisal.
steps.whatsHappening: Students suggest a reason for רב נחמן's statement. This sets up the correction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purpose of an announcement is to reach the fair price. The students thought expert judges could set the price without one. This guess will be rejected in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it (an assumption that is often corrected)
Experts in appraisal (valuing property)

steps.confusionAlert: This is only what the students assumed, not the final reason. The גמרא corrects it right away.

phrases.english: They understood from it
that it was because they were experts in appraisal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a reason for רב נחמן's statement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Assumed reason: the judges of נהרדעא were expert appraisers, so they did not need announcements

steps.title: The real reason: buyers at announced sales got an insulting nickname
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר מניומי says רב נחמן told him the real reason. People who bought at announced sales were mocked as people who eat up announced property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר מניומי said to them: It was explained to me by רב נחמן himself. It was because they called them 'people who eat up announced property.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף בר מניומי rejects the students' guess. He reports the reason he heard from רב נחמן himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Expertise was not the reason. Buyers at announced sales were looked down on as people who profit from someone else's trouble. Decent people stopped buying, so נהרדעא stopped announcing.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally
Eaters of announced property (an insulting nickname)

steps.whatToRemember: נהרדעא did not announce court sales because of the shame attached to buying announced property, not because its judges were expert appraisers.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said to them:
To me it was explained
by Rav Naḥman himself,
because they would call them
"people who eat up announced property."
phrases.notes: This was a put-down for buyers who jump at property sold because someone is in trouble.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the students' assumed reason and gives the true one
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reason, not רב נחמן's report itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The guess about expert appraisers is not what רב נחמן meant. The real reason was social shame.

steps.title: שמואל: orphans' movable property is appraised and sold right away
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the court appraises orphans' movable property and sells it immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Movable property of orphans is appraised and sold immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: how to sell movable property that belongs to orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Movable items can wear out or lose value over time. So שמואל says the court should value them and sell them without waiting. This protects the orphans' money.

keyTerms.meaning: Movable property
Orphans
They appraise (set the value)
Immediately

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Movable property of orphans —
they appraise it
and sell it immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִטַּלְטְלִין שֶׁל יְתוֹמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related topic about court sales for orphans
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Orphans' movable property is appraised and sold right away

steps.title: אבימי: orphans' movable property is sold at the market
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes אבימי: orphans' movable property is sold at the markets.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי: They sell it at the markets.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ruling on the same question, which seems to say something different from שמואל. This sets up the גמרא's next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Market day brings many buyers, so the items fetch a fair price. That seems to mean waiting for the market, while שמואל said to sell immediately.

keyTerms.meaning: Markets (market days, when many buyers come)

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said that Avimi said:
They sell it at the markets.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר אֲבִימִי מוֹכְרִין אוֹתָן לִשְׁוָוקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling that seems to conflict with שמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Orphans' movable property is sold on market day

steps.title: No real disagreement: it depends on how close market day is
steps.stepSummary: If market day is near, the court waits and sells at the market. If market day is far off, it sells immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree. This one is when the market is near. That one is when the market is far.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל and אבימי do not really argue. Each one is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When market day is close, waiting a little gets a better price, so אבימי's rule applies. When market day is far away, the items could lose value while waiting, so שמואל's rule applies. Both rules aim to protect the orphans.

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not disagree
Is near
Is far

steps.whatToRemember: Orphans' movable property is sold in the way that gets the best value: at the market if market day is near, and immediately if it is far off.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
this one is when the market is near,
phrases.notes: "This one" is אבימי, who says to sell at the market.

phrases.english: that one is when the market is far.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי הָא דִּמְיקָרַב שׁוּקָא הָא דִּמְרַחַק שׁוּקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the apparent conflict between steps 21 and 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by situation (how near market day is)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל and אבימי seem to argue about when to sell
steps.terutzMaskana: Sell at the market if it is near; sell immediately if it is far

steps.title: רב כהנא waits for the festival to sell an orphan's beer
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא held beer belonging to the orphan רב משרשיא בר חילקאי. He waited until the festival to sell it, because even with some spoilage it would bring good, ready money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא had beer belonging to an orphan, רב משרשיא בר חילקאי. He held it until the festival. He said: even if it spoils a little, at the festival it will bring in good cash.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the rule from the last step in action: if a good market time is coming, the orphan's goods are held for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said that when market day is close, the court waits and sells there. רב כהנא does exactly that. He accepts a small risk of spoilage because the festival crowds bring a higher price paid in cash, and that is better for the orphan.

keyTerms.meaning: Beer, often made from dates
An orphan
Festival, when crowds came and markets were busy
Some spoilage or souring
Literally 'sharp money': quick cash at a good price

phrases.english: Rav Kahana had beer in his hands
belonging to Rav Mesharshiyya bar Chilkai, an orphan.
He held it back until the festival.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: אַף עַל גַּב דְּנָפֵל בֵּיהּ אִיצְצָתָא,
phrases.english: He said: even though some spoilage may fall into it,
it brings in sharp money.
phrases.notes: 'Sharp money' means cash in hand at a good price, not a promise to pay later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real-life case showing the step 23 rule of waiting for a market that is close.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the court waits for a nearby market day before selling orphans' goods
steps.raayaSupportSource: What רב כהנא actually did with the orphan's beer

steps.title: רבינא asks whether he may sell his nephew's wine with his own
steps.stepSummary: רבינא held wine belonging to his orphaned nephew, רבינא זוטי. He was taking his own wine to סיכרא to sell and asked רב אשי whether he could bring the orphan's wine along too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא had wine belonging to the orphan רבינא זוטי, his sister's son. He also had wine of his own and was taking it up to סיכרא. He came to רב אשי and asked: may I bring the orphan's wine along with mine?
steps.whatsHappening: A second story begins. רבינא sets up a practical question for רב אשי about how to sell an orphan's wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא was unsure whether he could simply sell the orphan's wine on his own trip, or whether he had to wait for a better time just for the orphan. The question is whether a guardian may treat the orphan's goods the same way he treats his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine
His sister's son, his nephew
סיכרא, a place where wine was sold
To bring along

phrases.english: Ravina had wine in his hands
belonging to Ravina the younger, an orphan, his sister's son.
He also had wine of his own,
and he was taking it up to Sikhra.
He came before Rav Ashi
and said to him: May I bring it along with ours?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about selling orphans' goods, this time framed as a question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a guardian may sell the orphan's wine together with his own, the same way and at the same time

steps.title: רב אשי: Go, the orphan's wine is no better than yours
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי told רבינא to go ahead and take the orphan's wine along, since it is no better than his own wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go. It is no better than yours.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא's question with a yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבינא thinks this trip is the right way to sell his own wine, it is also a fine way to sell the orphan's wine. The guardian's honest judgment about his own goods is a good enough standard for the orphan's goods.

keyTerms.meaning: Go
It is no better
Than yours

steps.whatToRemember: Orphans' goods should be sold in a way that is good for them: wait for a nearby market (רב כהנא), and a guardian may sell them the same way he sells his own goods (רב אשי).

phrases.english: He said to him: Go,
it is no better than yours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל, לָא עֲדִיף מִדִּידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes: sell the orphan's wine with your own, since what is good enough for your wine is good enough for his.

steps.title: New משנה: three women who get no כתובה or other payments
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a ממאנת, a שניה, and an איילונית get no כתובה, no payment for produce, no food, and no worn clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A girl who refuses her marriage, a woman who is a rabbinically forbidden relative, and a woman who cannot have children do not get a כתובה, payment for produce, food, or their worn clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new משנה about three kinds of women who do not get the usual money owed at the end of a marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממאנת is a young orphan girl married off by her mother or brother who refuses the marriage once she grows up. A שניה is a relative forbidden by the rabbis, and an איילונית cannot have children. The משנה says none of them gets the כתובה or the three other benefits listed.

keyTerms.meaning: A young orphan girl who refuses her marriage when she grows up
A relative forbidden by the rabbis, a secondary forbidden relative
A woman who is physically unable to have children
Payment for produce the husband ate from her property
Worn-out clothes or items she brought into the marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Each of these women loses her rights for a different reason. Do not assume the משנה is saying all three are the same kind of case.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The one who refuses, the secondary relative, and the ailonit
do not have a ketubah,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא פֵּירוֹת וְלֹא מְזוֹנוֹת וְלֹא בְּלָאוֹת.
phrases.english: nor produce, nor food, nor worn clothes.
phrases.notes: 'Produce' means payment for what the husband ate from her fields. 'Worn clothes' means items from her dowry that wore out.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְמָאֶנֶת, הַשְּׁנִיָּה, וְהָאַיְלוֹנִית אֵין לָהֶן כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic; the discussion of orphans' property is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ממאנת, a שניה, and an איילונית get no כתובה, no payment for produce, no food, and no worn clothes.

steps.title: Marrying her knowing she is an אילונית
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds an exception: if the husband knew from the start that she was an אילונית, she does get a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he married her from the beginning knowing she was an אילונית, she gets a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits its earlier rule that an אילונית gets no כתובה. That rule does not apply if the husband knew the truth when he married her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה (step 27), an אילונית loses her כתובה. Here the משנה says that if the husband married her knowing what she was, she keeps it. She is still an אילונית; only the result is different.

keyTerms.meaning: from the start, at the time of the marriage
with the understanding that, knowing that
a woman who never develops the signs of maturity and cannot have children

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think she stops being an אילונית. She is still an אילונית; the only change is that she keeps her כתובה because he knew from the start.

phrases.english: If from the start he married her
knowing she was an אילונית
she has a כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the earlier rule of the משנה that an אילונית gets no כתובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אילונית whom the husband married knowing her condition is entitled to a כתובה.

steps.title: Women in forbidden marriages still get a כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists marriages the Torah forbids and rules that the women in them still get a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow married to a כהן גדול, a divorcee or a חלוצה married to a regular כהן, a ממזרת or a נתינה married to a regular Jew, and a Jewish woman married to a נתין or a ממזר all get a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with a list of forbidden marriages. In every one of them, the woman still gets her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These marriages are forbidden by the Torah, yet the משנה rules that the woman still gets her כתובה. This stands in contrast to the women in step 27, who get none. The משנה gives the rule without giving a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: the High Priest, who may not marry a widow
a woman released from יבום through חליצה
a regular כהן
a woman descended from the Gibeonites, who may not marry into ישראל
a woman born from a forbidden relationship

steps.whatToRemember: Being in a forbidden marriage does not by itself take away a woman's כתובה.

phrases.english: A widow married to a High Priest,
a divorcee or a חלוצה married to a regular כהן,
a ממזרת or a נתינה married to a regular Jew,
phrases.notes: The נתינים are the Gibeonites from the days of יהושע.

phrases.english: a Jewish woman married to a נתין or a ממזר
they all have a כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, גְּרוּשָׁה וַחֲלוּצָה לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets these women against the women in step 27: here the women do get a כתובה even though the marriage is forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women in marriages that are forbidden but still take effect are entitled to a כתובה.

steps.title: רב: a minor divorced with a גט gets no כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רב's version: a minor who leaves with a גט gets no כתובה, and a ממאנת certainly gets none.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב taught: a minor girl who leaves her marriage with a גט has no כתובה, and all the more so a ממאנת has none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and brings רב's version of a teaching about a minor girl. In his version, a minor who leaves with a גט gets no כתובה, and a ממאנת certainly gets none.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reasons from the stronger case to the weaker one, a קל וחומר. Leaving with a גט is the more serious way to end a marriage. If even that girl gets no כתובה, then a girl who simply refuses through מיאון surely gets none.

keyTerms.meaning: a minor girl
a bill of divorce
all the more so

phrases.english: GEMARA
רב taught:
a minor girl who leaves her marriage with a גט
has no כתובה.
And all the more so a ממאנת.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב תָּנֵי: קְטַנָּה — יוֹצְאָה בְּגֵט אֵין לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by explaining the ממאנת in the משנה and adding the case of a minor who leaves with a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, a minor who leaves with a גט has no כתובה, and a ממאנת all the more so.

steps.title: שמואל: only the ממאנת loses her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches a different version: a ממאנת gets no כתובה, but a minor who leaves with a גט does get one.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל taught: a ממאנת has no כתובה, but a girl who leaves with a גט has a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's version, which disagrees with רב about the minor who leaves with a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a ממאנת gets no כתובה. The disagreement is about a minor who is given a גט. רב says she gets nothing, while שמואל says she gets her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: but
leaves the marriage

steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל agree that a ממאנת gets no כתובה. They disagree only about a minor who leaves with a גט: רב says no כתובה, שמואל says yes.
steps.confusionAlert: Both רב and שמואל use the word ממאנת. The argument is not about her at all. It is only about the minor who leaves with a גט.

phrases.english: שמואל taught:
a ממאנת has no כתובה,
but one who leaves with a גט
has a כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל תָּנֵי: מְמָאֶנֶת — אֵין לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a version that disagrees with רב about the minor who leaves with a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, a ממאנת has no כתובה, but a minor who leaves with a גט does have one.

steps.title: שמואל is consistent with his own teaching elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that שמואל's view on the כתובה matches a statement he made elsewhere: a ממאנת gets no כתובה, but a woman who leaves with a גט does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל follows his own reasoning, as שמואל said: a girl who does מיאון has no כתובה. A girl who leaves with a גט does have a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל's ruling in the last step is not a one-time idea. He said the same thing in a larger teaching, which the גמרא now begins to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 31, שמואל said a minor who leaves with a גט gets a כתובה but a ממאנת does not. Here the גמרא brings his own words from another place saying exactly this. That shows his view rests on a steady principle: מיאון undoes the marriage, but a גט ends a real marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: And he follows his own reasoning (he is consistent with what he said elsewhere)
A girl married off as a minor who refuses the marriage (מִיאוּן), leaving without a גט
A woman who leaves the marriage through a bill of divorce
The marriage contract payment owed to a wife when the marriage ends

steps.confusionAlert: Both women here may be minors. The difference is not age. It is HOW the marriage ended: by refusal (מיאון) or by a גט.

phrases.english: And Shmuel follows his own line of reasoning,
as Shmuel said:
One who refuses — she has no marriage contract;
one who leaves with a bill of divorce — she has a marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's version from step 31 by showing he taught the same rule in another statement.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a minor divorced with a גט gets a כתובה but a ממאנת does not
steps.raayaSupportSource: A separate list of rules taught by שמואל contrasting a ממאנת with a woman who leaves with a גט

steps.title: A ממאנת is not forbidden to the brothers or to a כהן; a divorcée is
steps.stepSummary: Continuing שמואל's list: a ממאנת may still marry her husband's brothers and a כהן, but a woman who left with a גט is forbidden to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: A girl who does מיאון: the marriage does not forbid her to the husband's brothers, and does not forbid her to כהונה. A woman who leaves with a גט: she is forbidden to the brothers and forbidden to כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting שמואל's list. This rule adds two more differences between a ממאנת and a woman who leaves with a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since מיאון cancels the marriage as if it never happened, she was never really the brother's wife and never really a divorcée. So she may marry a brother of her ex-husband or a כהן. A גט ends a real marriage, so she counts as the brother's ex-wife and as a גרושה, who may not marry a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: He disqualified her (made her forbidden to marry someone)
The brothers (here: the husband's brothers)
The priesthood. Here it means she may marry a כֹּהֵן

steps.whyThisMatters: These rules show the core of the סוגיא. A ממאנת's marriage is undone entirely, and that is why she also gets no כתובה.

phrases.english: One who refuses — he did not disqualify her from the brothers,
and he did not disqualify her from the priesthood.
One who leaves with a bill of divorce — he disqualified her from the brothers,
and he disqualified her from the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same statement of שמואל begun in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ממאנת is permitted to her ex-husband's brothers and to a כהן. A woman who leaves with a גט is forbidden to both.

steps.title: A ממאנת does not need to wait three months
steps.stepSummary: Another item in שמואל's list: a ממאנת may remarry right away, without the three-month wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: A girl who does מיאון does not need to wait three months before remarrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues שמואל's list with another difference. A ממאנת does not have to wait three months before marrying again. The list keeps going after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a woman whose marriage ends must wait three months before remarrying. שמואל says the ממאנת is free of this wait. This fits the same pattern as before: her ending of the marriage is treated differently from a normal divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: To wait
Three months, the usual waiting period before a woman remarries

phrases.english: One who refuses does not need
to wait three months,
